ai_show_review.summary: Otherworldly Dark Star & ripping Not Fade Away jam dominate
ai_show_review.blurb: The second set erupts with a soaring Dark Star that flows into Saint Stephen, then rockets through a monster Not Fade Away → Darkness → China Cat sequence before an exuberant Turn On Your Lovelight finale. Jerry’s tone is on fire and the rhythm section drives the high‑energy peaks, while Morning Dew and Easy Wind provide early‑set highlights.
ai_show_review.review:
On September 19, 1970 at the Fillmore East, the Dead delivered a performance that has become a benchmark for the early‑70 era. Set two launches with a transcendent Dark Star, its improvisational sweep highlighted by Jerry’s soaring tone and tasteful wah‑wah flourishes, before slipping seamlessly into Saint Stephen and then detonating into a blistering Not Fade Away → Darkness → China Cat jam that still feels fresh decades later. The band rides this momentum straight into an uplifting Turn On Your Lovelight, closing the night on a high note. Earlier in the show, Morning Dew and Easy Wind showcase Phil’s thunderous bass foundation and the duo’s tight interplay, while the first set offers a solid run of roots‑rock numbers that set the stage for the second‑set fireworks.

Across all available sources the soundboard capture (gd70-09-19.sbd.kaplan.5217.sbeok.shnf) stands out as the definitive listening experience: an 80 % board mix with crystal‑clear instrument separation, only a faint scrape at the 16‑minute mark. This recording preserves every nuance of the band’s chemistry, making it the recommended version for both newcomers and seasoned Deadheads seeking to relive one of the most celebrated Fillmore nights.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: Four out of five recordings are strongly positive, repeatedly praising the Dark Star, Not Fade Away jam and overall band tightness; one mixed review notes only audio issues. Consistent high praise yields a robust positive sentiment adjustment.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard mix (80% board) with superb instrument separation; captures the full set including the legendary Dark Star and Not Fade Away → Darkness jam without significant flaws.

key_highlights: Otherworldly Dark Star that segues into Saint Stephen and launches a monster jam
Ripping Not Fade Away → Darkness → China Cat sequence
Uplifting Turn On Your Lovelight finale
Powerful Morning Dew and Easy Wind early‑set moments

band_performance.Jerry: His tone is on fire, especially during Dark Star where he adds soaring leads and a tasteful wah‑wah pedal, driving the improvisations with fierce energy.
band_performance.Phil: Delivers a thunderous bass foundation throughout, highlighted by a massive presence in Dark Star and a powerful opening bomb on Morning Dew.
band_performance.Bob: Provides tight dual‑guitar interplay, especially during the China Cat segment, adding depth and excitement to the jams.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums lock perfectly with the guitars, propelling the high‑energy peaks of Dark Star, Not Fade Away and Darkness jams.
band_performance.Billy: Shares a tight, driving partnership with Mickey, keeping the rhythm rock solid through extended improvisations.
